steel-blue caps for the second option title
light sans factor labels in caps
sans verdict paragraphs with caps lead-ins

t2i_prompt: Flat UI mockup, no device frame, of a comparison section for <CONTENT> on a deep navy ground inside a thin frame. A light wide uppercase question headline; two option titles left and right, the second in steel blue, meeting at a small circled VS node. A vertical centre spine runs down with numbered factor labels; at each factor, mirrored horizontal capsule bar gauges extend left and right with off-white fills and steel-blue end caps, small mono values and curved leader-line callouts. Two verdict paragraphs side by side at the bottom. 1 px off-white lines, symmetrical, no shadows, generous spacing.
signature_idea: Two routes mirrored across a spine of factors, each factor read as a pair of gauges, ending in a plain 'choose this when' verdict for each.
strengths: verdicts per route match how engineers actually choose
symmetry makes trade-offs readable at a glance
light headline and one steel-blue accent are on brand
weaknesses: bars imply quantitative scores the copy may not support
annotations and callouts are cluttered and illegible
rounded capsule bars break the square-corner rule
left-side bars missing on some rows look broken
brand_fit_why: Navy ground, light caps type, one steel-blue accent and mono values fit; rounded bars and annotation clutter work against square, calm precision.
